Moreover, this construction is much more efficient than the naive approach of padding execution time to the worst-case dataset size $n_{\textrm{max}}=2^{\omega}-1$ , which would result in slow runtimes for datasets with size $n<n_{\textrm{max}}$ . In the RAM model of computation, the construction yields a timing-private DP sum in the unbounded DP model.

### 6.3 Composition of Timing-Private Programs

We can treat the composition of timing-private mechanisms similarly to how we treat chaining. In particular, our framework supports the composition of timing-private programs that perform intermediate DP computations.

#### Definition 58 (Composition-compatible Programs).

We say that programs $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}$ and $P_{2}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}$ are composition-compatible if there is a program $P_{2}\otimes P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{Z})\times\mathcal{E}$ and a constant $c$ such that for all inputs $x\in\mathcal{X}$ and all execution environments $\mathtt{env}_{1}\in\mathcal{E}$ , there exists a (possibly random) input-compatible execution environment $\mathtt{env}_{2}\in\mathcal{E}$ such that we have:

$$ \displaystyle\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})),\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))),\mathtt{env}_{2}))) $$

and

$$ \displaystyle T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\otimes P_{1})}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))),\mathtt{env}_{2})+c. $$

Similar to the case of chaining-compatible programs, we allow the random variable $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ to be arbitrarily correlated with the output and runtime of $P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})$ , but it should be independent of the coin tosses of $P_{2}$ .

#### Lemma 59 (Composition-compatible Word RAM Programs).

Let program $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}$ be a RAM program that writes its unmodified input to

$$ \displaystyle M[\texttt{output\_ptr}],\dots,M[\texttt{output\_ptr}+\texttt{input\_len}-1] $$

and appends the rest of its output to $M[\texttt{output\_ptr}+\texttt{input\_len}]$ , $\dots$ , $M[\texttt{output\_ptr}+\texttt{output\_len}-1]$ . Then $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ are composition-compatible for all programs $P_{2}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{E}$ .

#### Proof.

The proof for composition-compatible programs works similarly to that of chaining-compatible programs. We replace the HALT at the end of $P_{1}$ to set $\texttt{input\_len}=\texttt{output\_len}$ and $\texttt{input\_ptr}=\texttt{output\_ptr}$ . The resulting program is an execution of $P_{2}$ on input $(x,y)$ in environment $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ that is the same as $\mathtt{out}\mathtt{env}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))$ except for these modifications to input_ptr and input_len. ∎

#### Remark 60.

The proof follows for RAM programs also.

#### Lemma 61 (Composition of OC-Timing-Stable Programs).

Let $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}$ be $(d_{1}\mapsto t_{1})$ -OC timing stable with respect to the $\mathcal{Y}$ output coordinate88 8 This means that we condition only on the $y\in\mathcal{Y}$ part of the output when considering OC-timing stability. and input distance metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ . Similarly, let $P_{2}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{Z})\times\mathcal{E}$ be $(d_{1}\mapsto t_{2})$ -OC timing stable with respect to input distance metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ on its first input coordinate. If $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ are composition compatible, then the composed program $P_{2}\otimes P_{1}$ is $(d_{1}\mapsto t_{1}+t_{2})$ -OC timing stable.

#### Proof.

For all $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{1}$ , all input-compatible environments $\mathtt{env}_{1},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , and all $(y,z)\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})))$ , we will construct a coupling $(\tilde{r},\tilde{r}^{\prime})$ of $T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\otimes P_{1})}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(y,z)}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\otimes P_{1})}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})|_{\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))=(y,z)}$ such that $|\tilde{r}-\tilde{r}^{\prime}|\leq t_{1}+t_{2}$ with probability $1$ .

Observe that for all $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ such that $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{1}$ , all $\mathtt{env}_{1},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , and all $(\cdot,y)\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})))$ , there exists a coupling $(\tilde{r}_{1},\tilde{r}_{1}^{\prime})$ of the conditional random variables $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(x,y)}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))=(x^{\prime},y)}$ such that $|\tilde{r}_{1}-\tilde{r}_{1}^{\prime}|\leq t_{1}$ (by the OC timing stability of $P_{1}$ ).

For all such $x,x^{\prime}$ and $\mathtt{env}_{1},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}$ , take $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ and $\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}$ to be the execution environments satisfying:

$$ \displaystyle T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\otimes P_{1})}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))),\mathtt{env}_{2})+c $$

and

$$ \displaystyle T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\otimes P_{1})}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x^{\prime},\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))),\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime})+c $$

respectively (such an $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ and $\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}$ exist due to $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ being composition-compatible). Now fix $y\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime})))$ . Then for all $z$ such that

$$ \displaystyle(y,z)\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}))) $$

there exists a coupling $(\tilde{r}_{2},\tilde{r}_{2}^{\prime})$ of the random variables $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2}))=(y,z)}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}))=(y,z)}$ such that $|\tilde{r}_{2}-\tilde{r}_{2}^{\prime}|\leq t_{2}$ (by the OC timing stability of $P_{2}$ ).

We sample $(r_{1},r_{1}^{\prime})\sim(\tilde{r}_{1},\tilde{r}_{1}^{\prime})$ and sample $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ conditioned on $(r_{1},y)$ and $\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}$ conditioned on $(r^{\prime}_{1},y)$ . We then samlpe $(r_{2},r_{2}^{\prime})\sim(\tilde{r}_{2},\tilde{r}_{2}^{\prime})|_{\mathtt{env}_{2},\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}}$ and let

$$ \displaystyle\tilde{r} \displaystyle=r_{1}+r_{2}+c \displaystyle=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=y}+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(y,z)}+c \displaystyle=T_{\scriptscriptstyle(P_{2}\otimes P_{1})}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(y,z)} $$

and similarly for $\tilde{r}^{\prime}$ , where $c$ is the constant in Definition 58. It follows that

$$ \displaystyle|\tilde{r}-\tilde{r}^{\prime}| \displaystyle=|r_{1}+r_{2}+c-r_{1}^{\prime}-r_{2}^{\prime}-c| \displaystyle=|r_{1}-r_{1}^{\prime}+r_{2}-r_{2}^{\prime}| \displaystyle\leq|r_{1}-r_{1}^{\prime}|+|r_{2}-r_{2}^{\prime}| \displaystyle\leq t_{1}+t_{2} $$

∎

Lemma 61 shows that we can reason about timing stability when composing DP programs. After analyzing the timing stability of the overall composed program, we can add a single timing delay to protect the release from timing attacks. Alternatively, we can compose timing-private programs such that composed program is also timing-private.

#### Lemma 62 (Composition of Timing-Private Programs).

Let $\mathcal{C}:(\mathcal{M}\times\mathcal{M})\to\mathcal{M}$ be a valid composition function for a privacy measure $M$ ; meaning that if $M(X_{1},X^{\prime}_{1})\leq d_{1}$ and $M(X_{2}|X_{1}=x,X^{\prime}_{2}|X^{\prime}_{1}=x^{\prime})\leq d_{2}$ then $M((X_{1},X_{2}),(X^{\prime}_{1},X^{\prime}_{2}))\leq C(d_{1},d_{2})$ . Let $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}$ be $(d_{0}\mapsto d_{1})$ -timing private with respect to its second output coordinate, input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ , and privacy measure $M$ . Let $P_{2}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{Z})\times\mathcal{E}$ be $(d_{0}\mapsto d_{2})$ -timing private with respect to its second output coordinate, input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ , and privacy measure $M$ . If $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ be composition compatible, then $P_{1}\otimes P_{2}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{Z})\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{0}\mapsto C(d_{1},d_{2}))$ -timing-private with respect to $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and privacy measure $M$ .

#### Proof.

By composition-compatibility, for all $x\in\mathcal{X}$ and input-compatible execution environments $\mathtt{env}_{1}$ , there exists an input-compatible execution environment $\mathtt{env}_{2}$ such that

$$ \displaystyle T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}\otimes P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})+T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))),\mathtt{env}_{2})+c $$

We can therefore analyze $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}\otimes P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})=(y,z)}$ using the joint random variable:

$$ \displaystyle(T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(x,y)},T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2}))=(y,z)}) $$

and similarly for $x^{\prime}$ . Since $P_{1}$ is timing-private with respect to input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and privacy measure $M$ , it follows that for all $d_{1}$ -close inputs $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ , all input-compatible execution environments $\mathtt{env}_{1},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1}$ , and all $y\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1})))$

$$ \displaystyle M(T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(x,y)},T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1}))=(x^{\prime},y)})\leq d_{1} $$

Similarly, since $P_{2}$ is timing-private with respect to input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and privacy measure $M$ , it follows that for all inputs $(x,y),(x^{\prime},y)\in\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$ that are $d_{1}$ -close on their first coordinate, all input-compatible execution environments $\mathtt{env}_{2},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{2}$ , and all $(y,z)\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{2})))$

$$ \displaystyle M(T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2}))=(y,z)},T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{2}))=(y,z)})\leq d_{2} $$

Let

$$ \displaystyle Y=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))=(x,y)} \displaystyle Y^{\prime}=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{1}}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1}))=(x^{\prime},y)} \displaystyle Z=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,y),\mathtt{env}_{2}))=(y,z)} \displaystyle Z^{\prime}=T_{\scriptscriptstyle P_{2}}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{2})|_{\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x^{\prime},y),\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{2}))=(y,z)} $$

Then

$$ \displaystyle M((Y,Z),(Y^{\prime},Z^{\prime})) \displaystyle\leq C(M(Y,Y^{\prime}),M(Z,Z^{\prime})) \displaystyle\leq C(d_{1},d_{2}) $$

which is what we wanted to show. ∎

The above composition theorem says that we can compose timing-private programs and keep track of the overall timing privacy guarantees. For example, $C((\varepsilon_{1},\delta_{1}),(\varepsilon_{2},\delta_{2}))=(\varepsilon_{1}+\varepsilon_{2},\delta_{1}+\delta_{2})$ is a valid composition function for approximate-DP (Lemma 23). Lemma 62 says that the composition of a program $P_{1}$ that is $(\varepsilon_{1},\delta_{1})$ -timing private with a program $P_{2}$ that is $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta_{2})$ -timing private, results in a new program that is $(\varepsilon_{1}+\varepsilon_{2},\delta_{1}+\delta_{2})$ -timing private.

We can use the above fact to construct timing-private programs, for example, that compute DP means from a timing-private DP sum program and a timing-private DP count program. #### Lemma 68.

Let $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}$ be the $\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP and $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta)$ -timing-private sum program (Lemma 57) that has been modified according to Remark 63. Let $P_{2}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ be the $\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP and $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta)$ -timing-private dataset count program (Lemma 67). Then $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ are composition-compatible.

#### Proof.

Observe that, due to the modifications from Remark 63, $P_{1}$ writes to its output the original dataset $x\in\mathcal{X}$ followed by the DP sum $y\in\mathbb{N}$ . By Lemma 59 the claim follows. ∎

#### Lemma 69.

Let $P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y})\times\mathcal{E}$ be the $\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP and $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta)$ -timing-private sum program (Lemma 57) that has been modified according to Remark 63. Let $P_{2}:(\mathcal{X}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ be the $\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP and $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta)$ -timing-private dataset count program (Lemma 67). Then $P_{2}\otimes P_{1}:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})\times\mathcal{E}$ is $2\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP and $(2\varepsilon_{2},2\delta)$ -timing-private.

#### Proof.

The first output coordinate of $P_{2}\otimes P_{1}$ is the output of $P_{1}$ , and the second output coordinate of $P_{2}\otimes P_{1}$ is the output of $P_{2}$ . Since $P_{1}$ is $\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP under input metric $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ and output metric $d_{\mathbb{N}}$ (Lemma 54), and $P_{2}$ is $\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP under input metric $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ and output metric $d_{\mathbb{N}}$ (Lemma 65), it follows that for all $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ satisfying $d_{\textrm{ID}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq 1$ , all input-compatible $\mathtt{env}_{1},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}_{1},\mathtt{env}_{2},\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , and all $(S_{1},S_{2})\subseteq(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})$ :

$$ \displaystyle\Pr[\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))\in(S_{1},S_{2})] \displaystyle\hskip-150.0pt=\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))\in S_{1}]\cdot\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x,\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x,\mathtt{env}_{1}))),\mathtt{env}_{2}))\in S_{2}] \displaystyle\hskip-150.0pt\leq e^{\varepsilon_{1}}\cdot\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))\in S_{1}]\cdot e^{\varepsilon_{2}}\cdot\Pr[\mathtt{out}(P_{2}((x^{\prime},\mathtt{out}(P_{1}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))),\mathtt{env}_{2}^{\prime}))\in S_{2}] \displaystyle\hskip-150.0pt\leq e^{\varepsilon_{1}+\varepsilon_{2}}\cdot\Pr[\mathtt{out}((P_{2}\otimes P_{1})(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}_{1}^{\prime}))\in(S_{1},S_{2})] $$

Therefore, $P_{2}\otimes P_{1}$ is $2\varepsilon_{1}$ -DP with respect to input metric $d_{\textrm{ID}}$ and the max-divergence privacy measure. The claim that $P_{2}\otimes P_{1}$ is $(2\varepsilon_{2},2\delta)$ -timing-private follows from the fact that $P_{1}$ is $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta)$ -timing-private, $P_{2}$ is $(\varepsilon_{2},\delta)$ -timing-private, and Lemma 62 and letting $C((\varepsilon,\delta),(\varepsilon,\delta))=(2\varepsilon,2\delta)$ be the composition function by Lemma 23. ∎

## 7 Implementation

A proof-of-concept implementation of our framework on top of the OpenDP library in available in the Github repository [SVM+]. The proof of concept supports defining timing stability maps for transformations and output-conditional timing stability maps for measurements. We additionally implemented a proof-of-concept timing-private delay function that can be chained with arbitrary output-conditional timing stable measurements to delay their output release.

The purpose of the implementation is to illustrate the compatibility of our framework with existing differential privacy libraries, not to claim that the implementation provides timing privacy for physical executions. As discussed in Section 1.2, we leave for future work the problem of instantiating our framework for physical timing channels, which would involve constraining the execution environment, identifying the appropriate units to measure timing, and finding realistic upper bounds on actual timing-stability constants.

## Appendix A Stability Proofs

#### Lemma 70.

A program $P:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto 0)$ -timing-stable if for all pairs of inputs $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ , and all input-compatible execution environments $\mathtt{env},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})\equiv T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})$ .

#### Proof.

For any two inputs $x$ and $x^{\prime}$ , take the coupling $(\tilde{r},\tilde{r}^{\prime})$ to be $(T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env}),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env}))$ . Since $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})\equiv T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})$ , it follows that the marginal distributions of $\tilde{r}$ and $\tilde{r}^{\prime}$ are identical to $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})$ , and $|\tilde{r}-\tilde{r}^{\prime}|=0$ . ∎

#### Lemma 71.

If $P:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ satisfies for all $x\in\mathcal{X}$ , $\mathtt{env}\in\mathcal{E}$ , $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})=c$ for some constant $c$ , then $P$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto 0)$ -timing stable.

#### Proof.

Since $P$ is constant time, $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})=c$ for all $x$ and $\mathtt{env}$ , then for all $x,x^{\prime}$ and input-compatible $\mathtt{env},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}$ , $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})\equiv T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})$ and the claim follows from Lemma 70. ∎

#### Lemma 72.

If $P:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ is deterministic (in its output) and is $(d_{in}\mapsto t_{out})$ -timing stable, then $P$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto t_{out})$ -OC-timing stable.

#### Proof.

For all $x$ and $x^{\prime}$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{in}$ , and any pair of environments $\mathtt{env},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , either $\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))\neq\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))$ or $\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))=\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))$ . If $\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))\neq\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))$ , then there is no requirement on the distributional closeness of $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})$ and the claim is satisfied. Now suppose that $\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))=\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))=y$ . By the timing stability of $P$ there exists a coupling $(\tilde{r},\tilde{r}^{\prime})$ of the random variables $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})$ such that $|\tilde{r}-\tilde{r}^{\prime}|\leq t_{out}$ . Since $P$ is deterministic it also follows that $\tilde{r}$ and $\tilde{r}^{\prime}$ have the same marginal distributions as $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})_{|\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))=y}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime})_{|\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))=y}$ respectively, and the claim holds. ∎

#### Lemma 73.

If $P:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ has constant runtime then $P$ is $(d_{in}\to 0)$ -OC timing stable.

#### Proof.

Since $P$ is constant time, $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})=c$ for all $x$ and $\mathtt{env}$ . For all $y\in\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env})))\cap\textrm{supp}(\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})))$ with $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{in}$ , let the coupling $(\tilde{r},\tilde{r}^{\prime})$ of $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})_{|\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))=y}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})_{|\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))=y}$ take the value $(c,c)$ . Then $\tilde{r}$ and $\tilde{r}^{\prime}$ are identically distributed to $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})_{|\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))=y}$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})_{|\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))=y}$ respectively, and $|\tilde{r}-\tilde{r}^{\prime}|=|c-c|=0$ . ∎

#### Lemma 74.

Jointly output/timing-stable programs are timing-stable programs.

#### Proof.

If $P:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto\{d_{out},t_{out}\})$ -jointly output/timing stable with respect to input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ , then for every $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{in}$ and all pairs of execution environments $\mathtt{env},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , there exists a coupling $((\tilde{u},\tilde{r}),(\tilde{u}^{\prime},\tilde{r}^{\prime}))$ of the joint random variables $(\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env}))$ and $(\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))$ satisfying $\Pr[|\tilde{r}-\tilde{r}^{\prime}|<t_{out}]=1$ . Take $(\tilde{r},\tilde{r}^{\prime})$ to be the coupling of the random variables $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env})$ and $T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})$ and the claim follows. ∎

#### Lemma 75.

Jointly output/timing-stable programs are output-stable programs.

#### Proof.

If $P:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{Y}\times\mathcal{E}$ is $(d_{in}\mapsto\{d_{out},t_{out}\})$ -jointly output/timing stable with respect to input metric $d_{\mathcal{X}}$ and output metric $d_{\mathcal{Y}}$ , then for every $x,x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{X}}(x,x^{\prime})\leq d_{in}$ and all pairs of execution environments $\mathtt{env},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{E}$ , there exists a coupling $((\tilde{u},\tilde{r}),(\tilde{u}^{\prime},\tilde{r}^{\prime}))$ of the joint random variables $(\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x,\mathtt{env}))$ and $(\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime})),T_{\scriptscriptstyle P}(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))$ satisfying $d_{\mathcal{Y}}(\tilde{u},\tilde{u}^{\prime})\leq d_{out}$ with probability $1$ . Take $(\tilde{u},\tilde{u}^{\prime})$ to be the coupling of the random variables $\mathtt{out}(P(x,\mathtt{env}))$ and $\mathtt{out}(P(x^{\prime},\mathtt{env}^{\prime}))$ and the claim follows. ∎
